title: Vaisakhi: 1699, 1919 and today
hook: one day that holds the Khalsa's birth, a massacre, and a harvest

segments.voice: Yesterday, Hola, and your line was ride in joy. Did you do one hard thing with a lighter heart? Today the calendar of memory comes to a day that gathers several of this year's stories at once. Day one thousand fifty-six.

Three scenes, one day. In the fields, wheat falls to the sickle. In the gurdwaras, Sikhs sing the birthday of the Khalsa. And in Amritsar, some people stand quietly in a walled garden. Guru Nanak has a line in the Asa di Var that sounds strange on a festival: suffering became the medicine, and comfort the disease. Vaisakhi is a day that can hold it. The title of today's lesson carries two years and a word: the year tradition gives for the Khalsa's birth, the year of the garden, and today. Today: Vaisakhi.
screen: `THREE SCENES, ONE DAY.` → `SUFFERING, THE MEDICINE.` → `TWO YEARS AND A WORD.`

segments.voice: This path has spent whole days on each of these. Today, hold them in one hand. First, birth. At Anandpur, on Vaisakhi, Guru Gobind Singh called for those who would give their heads, and the five beloved stood up. The amrit was stirred, and the Khalsa was born. That's the first year in the title, the date tradition gives. Second, grief. On a Vaisakhi much later, troops fired on an unarmed gathering in Jallianwala Bagh, the garden this path stood in a week ago. That's the second year. Third, harvest. Long before either, Vaisakhi was the harvest day in Punjab, when the wheat comes in, and tradition says Guru Amar Das asked the Sikhs to gather at Vaisakhi. The harvest comes every year, whatever else happened. That's the last word in the title: today. Fourth, why one day can hold all three. In the Asa di Var on Ang 469, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase, that suffering became the medicine and comfort the disease, because when there is comfort, the One is forgotten. He isn't praising pain. On one reading, he's saying hardship can keep the One in mind, where comfort lets the One slip away. On Vaisakhi, the harvest and the birth are celebrated fully, and the grief is not pushed out of the room. Each keeps the others honest. Joy without memory would forget the garden. Memory without joy would forget the Khalsa's birthday and the wheat. So the same day holds kirtan, langar, processions, and, in Amritsar, silence in a garden. That's today's line: birth, grief, harvest.
screen: `BIRTH: THE KHALSA AT ANANDPUR.` · `GRIEF: THE GARDEN.` · `HARVEST: THE WHEAT COMES IN.` · `ANG 469: SUFFERING, THE MEDICINE.` · then, large: `BIRTH, GRIEF, HARVEST.`

segments.voice: Give thanks for three things. Sit, and breathe slowly. On the first long breath, bring to mind something new in your life, something just born: a friendship, a habit, an idea. Give thanks for it. On the next, something you've lost or grieved. Not to reopen it, just to honor that it mattered. Give thanks that you were able to love it. On the third, something that's ready, a harvest: work finished, a season you came through. Give thanks for it too. If you pray, you can say Waheguru after each one. Then rest with all three. The bell holds the time.
Vaisakhi. The day that holds the Khalsa's birth, the grief of Jallianwala Bagh, and the harvest, all at once. Today's word.
Your line: birth, grief, harvest. Today, tell one person about something good that's begun for you, and one thing you're still missing. Let both be true. Day one thousand fifty-six.

howItsDone: On Vaisakhi, Sikhs gather in gurdwaras for kirtan and Ardas, celebrate the founding of the Khalsa with nagar kirtan processions and langar, and in Punjab mark the wheat harvest. In Amritsar, people also visit the Jallianwala Bagh memorial.

match.prompt: one day, three memories — tap the pairs.

myth: Vaisakhi became a gathering day only with the Khalsa
it was already the harvest day, and tradition says Guru Amar Das asked the Sikhs to gather then.
in Ang 469, Guru Nanak is praising pain
he says that when there is comfort, the One is forgotten. on one reading, hardship keeps the One in mind.
the harvest is part of Vaisakhi whatever else the year held
the wheat comes in every year, whatever else happened.

fork.setup: a friend says Vaisakhi is just a harvest holiday. what does today's lesson add?
options: it also holds the Khalsa's birth and the grief of the garden.
it's only about the Khalsa now.
fork.reveal: one day holds three: birth, grief and harvest. Guru Nanak's line on Ang 469 is one way to hear how grief can sit inside a festival without ruling it.

original.note: Gurmukhi: Khalsa, the order Guru Gobind Singh founded at Vaisakhi.

trapdoor: what you thought: a harvest holiday.

what a scholar hears: Guru Nanak's Asa di Var on Ang 469, suffering the medicine and comfort the disease, which lets a festival carry its grief without being ruled by it.
